question: How does Catholic moral theology distinguish 'formal' from 'material' cooperation with evil?

choices.A: Formal cooperation shares in the evil intention of the primary agent and is always illicit; material cooperation provides assistance without sharing the intention and may sometimes be permissible with proportionate reason
choices.B: Formal cooperation is cooperation by clergy; material cooperation is cooperation by laypeople
choices.C: Formal cooperation is direct physical involvement; material cooperation is any moral support
choices.D: Both types of cooperation are always equally sinful and must always be avoided

teaching.title: Formal vs. Material Cooperation with Evil
teaching.body: Cooperation with evil is unavoidable in complex societies. The key distinction: Formal cooperation — the cooperator shares the evil intention of the principal agent (e.g., a getaway driver who approves of the robbery). This is always morally wrong. Material cooperation — the cooperator provides assistance without sharing the evil intention (e.g., a bank teller forced to hand over money to armed robbers). Material cooperation may be permissible depending on: (1) proximity to the evil act; (2) proportionate reason; (3) availability of alternatives. This framework is used in bioethics (e.g., whether a Catholic hospital may allow a procedure it opposes).
refs: Grisez, The Way of the Lord Jesus, Vol. 2
